name: Workload-Centric Analysis Framework
definition: A framework to connect individual optimizations with their system effects by tracing the forward rendering path through five specific counts: Nresident, Nactive, Npair, Neval, and Nblend.
summary: The Workload-Centric Analysis Framework connects rendering optimizations to systemic effects by tracing five workload counts, providing a backend-agnostic abstraction that isolates algorithmic costs from hardware details.
